title: embeddings-rerank-dim-mismatch-latency-scratch
content:
Purpose:
- Scratchpad for the embedding + rerank endpoint anomalies (dim mismatch errors seen intermittently + latency spikes on rerank pipeline). Notes for triage and repro attempts.

Symptoms observed:
- Dimension mismatch exceptions in rerank service logs: "ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 768, got 512". Happens ~1-2x/day, correlated with brief latency spikes on /v1/rerank endpoint (p95 from ~120ms -> 700-1200ms).
- Spike windows last ~30s-3m, then back to normal. No host OOMs observed.
- Affected customers: internal repro tenant + 3 paying customers (CS alerted).

First-pass hypotheses:
1) Model artifact mismatch: some rolling deploy pushed a 512-d model variant while caller expects 768.
2) Feature/transform bug: upstream embedding service occasionally returns 512-d embeddings due to fallback model or cached embedding vector.
3) Request routing: traffic routed to different model shard (quantized variant) with different dimension.
4) Serialization/truncation bug: vector serialization lost last 256 dims in some code path (gzip/chunk boundary).
5) Client-side: some clients sending pre-computed embeddings (512d) to rerank endpoint that expects 768d.

Quick checks done (timestamps in UTC):
- 2026-02-25 14:12:40 - saw first error in staging logs. grep on rerank-service logs: 
  
  2026-02-25T14:12:40Z ERROR rerank.service: Exception while scoring batch id=abc123
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/app/rerank/serve.py", line 202, in score_batch
      scores = model.score(queries_emb, candidates_emb)
  ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 768, got 512

- Matched the batch id to request payload in access logs (nginx + edge): client was internal-test-job (no precomputed embeddings). Call went through /internal/batch-rerank route.
- 2026-02-25 14:12:32 - embedding-service logs for same request: returned embeddings shape (batch_size=8, dim=768) according to debug logs. But rerank process read 512. Indicates mismatch after handoff (serialization / queue).

Repro attempts / commands run:
- Local integration repro (python):
  (venv) $ python -c "import requests, json; req={'queries':[\"q1\"], 'candidates':[[\"doc1\"]]}; print(requests.post('https://staging.api.redwood/v1/rerank', json=req).text)"
  -> No error on single-run.

- Replay of original nginx access log with same headers/body to staging endpoint (curl):
  $ curl -v -H 'X-Request-Id: abc123' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d @payload.json https://staging.api.redwood/v1/rerank
  -> Response OK when replayed.

- Capture thrift/s3/redis handoffs: rerank uses redis LPOP queue for async batching. Pulled raw payload from redis for the failing window:
  $ redis-cli -u redis://cache-01 get batch:abc123 -> payload bytes (base64). Decoded and inspected length: expected 8*768*4 bytes ~24576 bytes. Actual length ~16384 bytes -> corresponds to 512 dims.

- Checked embedding-service push to redis (producer side): embedding service publishes serialized payload to redis list. Found intermittent code path: if model vendor == 'fast-embed-v1' then we pack as float16 (2 bytes) vs default float32 (4 bytes) and set metadata.dim. There's a bug where metadata.dim is set to 768 always for compatibility, but actual float16 pack uses 512 dims (fast-embed-v1 produces 512 float16 dims). So consumer interprets as 768x4 float32 length and ends up reading only part -> leads to ValueError.

Root cause (working hypothesis):
- Recent onboarding of fast-embed-v1 (smaller model, 512 float16 output) introduced a serialization mismatch: producer wrote float16 vectors without setting correct dim/format header or set wrong metadata, and consumer always assumes float32/768. Race condition: producer sometimes falls back to fast-embed-v1 under high load (latency-targeted fallback) -> explains intermittent nature.

Why latency spikes?
- When consumer detects mismatch it catches error and falls back to synchronous in-process embedding computation or re-fetch path, causing extra latency per batch. Also failed batches trigger retry paths and blocking on single-host queue: p95 increases.

Evidence supporting this hypothesis:
- Found commit in PR #814 that added fast-embed-v1 fallback logic to embedding-service (linked above). Author: alex-rivera. Deployed 2026-02-24 03:00 UTC.
- Redis payload sizes during windows match 512-d float16 length.
- Consumer logs show fallback code path triggering immediately after mismatch events.

Immediate mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2026-02-25 16:20 UTC: added temporary middleware on rerank consumer to validate metadata.dim against actual byte length and reject with a clear log + drop instead of attempting fallback. Patch: revert-fast-fallback-hotfix (hotfix ref #INFR-2473-hotfix). Result: incident frequency dropped but some clients observed 4xxs.
- 2026-02-26 02:10 UTC: rolled back fast-embed-v1 fallback from embedding-service in staging and canary hosts. Monitoring p95 returned to baseline in canary.

Next permanent fixes (actions):
- Fix serialization contract: producer must always set metadata fields correctly and include dtype tag (float32/float16) and dim. Consumer must validate and support both dtype/dim combinations explicitly. (Owner: Alex Rivera, high priority).
- Add end-to-end test that simulates fast-embed-v1 paths with both float16/float32 packing and ensures consumer decoding succeeds. (Owner: Liam Chen).
- Improve observability: instrument redis payload headers in infra logs; add metric: embedding_payload_dim_mismatch_count; alert at >1/min for 5m. (Owner: SRE).
- Migration plan: staged rollout of corrected producer + consumer in canary -> 10% -> 100%. Add a compatibility shim that converts float16->float32 at consumer if header present.
- Add stronger contract to model catalog: each model entry must list output_dim and dtype. Reject fallback to incompatible model unless consumer advertises support. (Product + infra).

Questions / open items:
- Why was metadata.dim hard-coded to 768 in the fast-embed-v1 adapter? Was it an oversight or deliberate compatibility hack? (Ping Alex)
- There are some older clients that submit precomputed embeddings directly to rerank (via /v1/rerank with embeddings field). Need to audit whether we validate those payloads.
- Can we add a short term on-host validation that, if dtype=float16 and dim=512, consumer transparently converts to float32 and pads/validates shape instead of failing? Risk: silent correctness issues.

Repro steps (for infra/eng to run locally):
1) check out branch alex/fix-embed-serializer (PR #814 local repro).
2) start local redis, run embedding-producer with config: MODEL_FALLBACK=fast-embed-v1, PACK_AS=float16.
3) run rerank-consumer that assumes 768 float32. Observe ValueError on consumer logs.
4) apply hotfix patch (validate header -> convert) and confirm success.

Useful commands (from my shell history):
- Pull redis payload: redis-cli -u $REDIS_URL lrange rerank-queue 0 10 | jq -r .[0] | base64 --decode > payload.bin
- Inspect length: $ python -c "import os; print(os.path.getsize('payload.bin'))"
- Decode float16 preview: $ python -c "import numpy as np; b=open('payload.bin','rb').read(); arr=np.frombuffer(b,dtype=np.float16); print(arr.shape)"
- Run local consumer: $ docker-compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up rerank-consumer

Notes for postmortem doc:
- Timeline of events with concrete timestamps (derive from logs).
- Root cause: incompatible serialization/metadata between embedding-producer and rerank-consumer introduced by fast-embed-v1 fallback.
- Impact: minor customer-facing errors (+ dropped requests) and temporary latency spikes during incident windows.
- Mitigations: rollback & hotfix applied, permanent fix planned.

People to loop in for PM/exec summary: 
- Product owner: Priya Kumar
- Head of Eng: Samir Gupta
- SRE lead: Jonah Park

Short-term owner assignments:
- Maya (me): coord triage, gather exact list of affected customers, collect payload samples, prepare timeline.
- Alex Rivera: patch producer adapter + unit tests.
- Liam Chen: add consumer validation + conversion shim + end-to-end tests.
- Jonah Park / SRE: add metric + alert, run canary rollout.

Misc notes / brain dump:
- Could also be related to quantization pipeline change we merged last week; check release notes for any dtype/dim expectations.
- Need to add clearer docs for model catalog fields (output_dim, dtype, packing).
- Consider adding schema validation on the redis payloads with a compact header (magic + version + dtype + dim + length) to avoid silent mismatches.

Next steps (today):
- 09:30 standup: sync with Alex + Liam + Jonah.
- 11:00 deploy consumer validation shim to canary.
- 15:00 prepare short postmortem draft with timeline and customer impact.

End of scratchpad.

---- raw snippets copied for reference ----
- Error line: ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 768, got 512
- Redis payload sizes observed: 24576 (expected 8*768*4) vs 16384 (8*512*4) but float16 case is actually 8*512*2 = 8192 bytes; observed 16384 suggests mixed packing in some windows. Need more payload samples.
- Candidate fixes in PRs: #814 (fast-embed fallback), #821 (consumer validation shim, WIP).

Saved payload samples dir: gs://redwood-incident-dumps/INFR-2473/samples/ (ask infra for access)
